newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sees one mln bpd oil output by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sees one mln bpd oil output by 2000.

text.p: Planned development of Algeria's oil and gas industry will increase crude output to one million barrels per day (bpd) and 60 billion cubic metres of gas annually by the year 2000, Algerian officials said on Friday.
Algeria, an OPEC member with a quota of 750,000 bpd and production estimated at 830,000 bpd in August, earns over 95 percent of its foreign exchange from energy exports.

Nazim Zouioueche, general manager of oil and gas giant Sonatrach, said on Algerian radio on Friday that nearly two thirds of needed investment was available, and would raise oil production to around one million bpd within four years.

A report drawn up by the office of Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and released on Friday, put investment needed for the energy development plan at $8 billion, plus 300 billion dinars in local currency ($5.4 billion).
The report is to go as a working paper to a conference on economic development and social policy, due to open on Sunday in Algiers.

"For the development of discovered but as yet unexploited gas fields, Sonatrach is preparing a vast programme of development of a dozen wet gas fields situated southeast of Hassi R'mel, in partnership with foreign companies," the report said.
The programme would also extend to dry gas fields, further south, in In-Salah region.
Hassi R'mel, deep in the Sahara, is Algeria's main gas field. A pipeline, with a capacity of 9.5 billion cubic metres a year, taking gas to Spain and Portugal is due to come on stream in November.
The report said Algeria's development strategy was based on four elements:
-- Relaunch of exploration efforts already underway;
-- Development of gas fields already discovered but not exploited;
-- Increased output at existing producing fields,
-- Rise in Algeria's natural gas export capacity.

This strategy, part of Sonatrach's medium-term planning, should result in doubled exports of natural gas, increasing them to 60 billion cubic metres annually around the year 2000, said the report, carried by Algeria's official news agency APS.

"For the period 1995-99, hydrocarbon production should pass from 164 million tonnes of oil equivalent (toe) to 180 million toe. Commercialised production will increase by 37 percent to reach 137 million toe in 1999, of which 23.4 percent will be for the domestic market.
"Production of crude oil will rise from 35 million toe to 40 million toe, of which 15 percent will come from new fields being worked in association (with foreign companies)," said the report.
"This development plan will need $8 billion and 300 billion dinars. More than 65 percent of this sum will be to develop the chain of gas-liquefied natural gas-condensate production."
Last Tuesday, Sonatrach signed a $177 million agreement with U.S. firms Anadarko Petroleum Corp and Halliburton Co to develop the southern oilfield of Hassi Berkine.
Doubling natural gas exports "was already a reality on the commercial level since contractual engagements have reached 59 billion cubic metres a year," the report said.
Algeria's energy exports earn it around $10 billion a year.
($1= 55 dinars)
